findings.finding: The scene is declared no-material-claims, but content/080-clinical-wrap-up.md teaches the quantitative relation D = D0 + Rt, defines its variables and units, imposes t >= 0, states that applying operations to both sides preserves equality, rearranges the relation for R, and records the restriction t != 0. These are quantitative, definitional, and model-boundary teaching claims, including a direct application of claim-unit-independent-rearrangement. Omitting the scene from claims.json and omitting a same-scene source note leaves this outcome-relevant application outside the candidate's evidence map.
findings.resolution: Change scene-clinical-wrap-up to claims-mapped; map its equality-preserving and restriction content to claim-unit-independent-rearrangement or an appropriately scoped replacement claim; add the scene ID to the retained claim record; and add a learner-visible source note in content/080-clinical-wrap-up.md listing every source attached to the mapped claims while clearly identifying the infusion model and values as invented.

findings.finding: The scene uses hr and mg/hr as unit symbols. NIST's standardized symbol for hour is h, yielding mg/h for the rate. The present notation is understandable and does not change the arithmetic, but it is inconsistent with the unit conventions used as authority elsewhere in this quantity-equation lesson.
findings.resolution: Use h and mg/h consistently throughout the clinical wrap-up, including the givens, solved time, and substitution check.

findings.finding: Independent recalculation confirms the assessment answer logic: item-linear-both-sides gives x = 7; item-fraction-equation gives x = 62/5 and substitutes to 5; item-classify-equation reduces to -6 = 1 and therefore has no solution; item-rearrange-formula gives h = 2A/b - k with b != 0; and item-transfer-counter gives n = 22 for T = 73 while 22.4 satisfies the separate T = 74 equation but violates the integer domain.
findings.resolution: No change required to these answer keys or domain classifications.

findings.finding: Direct inspection of NIST sections 7.1 and 7.11 confirms the cited distinction: quantity equations relate quantities and are independent of the units chosen, whereas numerical-value equations depend on the units used. This supports claim-quantity-equation and claim-numerical-equation within their declared scopes.
findings.resolution: No change required to these two claims or their cited locator.

limitations: Cross-course terminology alignment and generated graph-node metadata were not verified because the material instructions prohibited reading site/ and scripts/; the permitted course syllabus search did not expose the two declared graph IDs. This did not prevent a responsible verdict on the lesson's elementary algebra, dimensional reasoning, evidence mapping, or assessment logic.

Repository and review-schema validation were not run because those commands would read prohibited scripts/ and site/ paths. The artifact was structured from the required academic review template, but automated validation remains for the operator.
